name: Term Purse
tagline: Make the loan drop last until the next one
about: Term Purse turns each student loan or grant instalment into a weekly allowance that survives the whole term, plans around rent day and exam weeks, and finds the part-time hours that pay without wrecking your grades.
persona: You are a straight-talking student money mentor: you know rent eats the loan first, you never lecture about coffee, and you plan in weeks not months.

onboarding.title: Stretch the drop
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us when money lands and what rent costs; we do the weekly maths.
bullets: Part-time hours that fit your timetable

tools.title: Stretch this instalment
tools.subtitle: Lump sum → weekly allowance
tools.prompt: Instalment {amount} must last {weeks} weeks with the profile's monthly rent and these fixed costs: {fixed}. Sections: kv (total fixed for the period, safe-to-spend total, weekly allowance, a 'panic line' balance you must not go under before the next drop); table (Week | Opening balance | Rent/fixed due | Allowance | Closing balance) with one row per week; a callout on the two weeks most likely to blow the plan (arrival/freshers week, exam week, birthdays) and how much to hold back for them; bullets of 3 ways to cut the weekly figure if the allowance is under what you can live on.

tools.title: Part-time hours math
tools.subtitle: How many shifts you actually need
tools.prompt: Shortfall {gap} per month at {wage} per hour with a {load} course load. Sections: kv (hours per month needed, hours per week, shifts per week at 4-hour shifts, a maximum safe weekly cap for this course load); cards for 4 student-friendly job types (meta = typical hourly · flexibility · exam-season friendliness); a callout on the weekly hours where grades typically start to slide and how to raise exam weeks with a manager; a quote with a message asking for reduced hours during exams.

tools.title: Course kit on a budget
tools.subtitle: Textbooks, software, equipment

inputs.label: Reading list / kit list
inputs.placeholder: Organic Chemistry 9th ed, lab coat, graphics calculator, Adobe CC…

tools.prompt: Kit list: {list}. Budget: {budget}. Sections: table (Item | Buy new | Used / older edition | Borrow / library / free alternative | Recommended route | Est. cost); a checklist of where to look, in order (library reserve, department loan, student-union sales, older editions, student software licences); a callout on the items you genuinely should not skimp on; kv (total at the recommended route vs budget, saving vs buying everything new).

tools.title: Money ran out
tools.subtitle: Get to the next drop safely
tools.prompt: Only {left} left with {days} days to go and bills due: {owed}. Sections: steps in priority order for the next 48 hours (talk to accommodation office or landlord about a later rent date, university hardship fund, arranged-overdraft rules, food bank or community pantry, selling or pausing subscriptions); a checklist of what to gather for a hardship-fund application; a quote with an email to the university hardship or student-money team explaining the situation in under 120 words; a callout listing what NOT to do (payday loans, stacking buy-now-pay-later, ignoring rent) and reminding that student support services are confidential.

tools.title: Summer gap plan
tools.subtitle: No loan over the break
tools.prompt: Summer: {weeks} weeks, plan: {plan}, monthly costs {costs}. Sections: kv (total summer cost, income needed, target savings to carry into next term, weekly allowance); table (Month | Income | Rent/costs | Save toward term | Notes); bullets on summer-only costs students forget (rent on an empty room, storage, travel home, local-tax rules for students); a callout on whether a summer sublet or a shorter contract makes sense for the profile.

disclaimer: General information, not financial, tax or legal advice; rules, thresholds and entitlements differ by country and change — confirm with official sources or a regulated adviser before acting.
